title: LazyDP: Co-Designing Algorithm-Software for Scalable Training of Differentially Private Recommendation Models
problem: DP-SGD training of recommender systems suffers from severe compute bottlenecks in noise sampling and memory bandwidth limitations in gradient updates. These bottlenecks cause significant performance overhead that prevents practical deployment of private recommendation systems at scale.
motivation: Differential privacy is an industry standard for privacy protection, but training large-scale recommender systems with DP-SGD remains computationally prohibitive, limiting practical adoption.
method: LazyDP uses algorithm-software co-design to optimize two key DP-SGD stages: it reduces compute overhead in noise sampling through algorithmic improvements and addresses memory bandwidth limitations in the noisy gradient update phase through software optimizations. The approach maintains mathematical equivalence with standard DP-SGD while achieving 119× speedup through these targeted optimizations.
key_novelty: Joint algorithm-software co-design that specifically targets compute and memory bandwidth bottlenecks in DP-SGD's noise sampling and gradient update stages for recommender systems.
contributions: Detailed characterization and root-cause analysis of DP-SGD performance bottlenecks in private recommender system training
LazyDP co-design approach optimizing noise sampling compute efficiency and gradient update memory bandwidth
119× training throughput improvement over state-of-the-art DP-SGD systems
Mathematically equivalent privacy guarantees enabling practical deployment of private recommender models
primary_theme: algorithm-software codesign for private recommender training
